title: Kiwoom Sees Hanwha Aerospace Hitting $3.3B Operating Profit in 2026 on Export Growth
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · September 30, 2026

Kiwoom Securities maintained a Buy rating and a target price of ₩1.58 million on Hanwha Aerospace, forecasting 2026 operating profit of ₩4.57 trillion, up 48% year over year, as export contracts spread from Poland to Northern Europe and a U.S. Army prototype selection opens a path to the American market. Here is what's behind the estimate and which export wins are already signed versus still pending.

CompanyRoleEvidence
Hanwha Aerospace
KRX: 012450		K9 self-propelled howitzer and Chunmoo multiple rocket launcher exporterFiling/Reported (export contracts and U.S. Army selection); earnings figures are analyst estimates

What Kiwoom Securities forecasts

  • Rating: Buy maintained, target price ₩1.58 million, published September 30. The stock closed at ₩1,012,000 on September 29.
  • Q3 2026 estimate: revenue ₩7.367 trillion (+13.6% year over year), operating profit ₩1.195 trillion (+39.5%).
  • Full-year 2026 estimate: revenue ₩32.04 trillion (+20.0%), operating profit ₩4.57 trillion (+48.0%) — the figure behind the "4.5 trillion won club" framing.
  • 2027 estimate: revenue ₩34.97 trillion, operating profit ₩6.10 trillion.
  • Order backlog: ₩38.3 trillion at the end of H1 2026, up 3% from the ₩37.2 trillion projected for year-end 2025.

Which export deals are confirmed

In 2026, Hanwha Aerospace signed Chunmoo multiple rocket launcher supply contracts with Norway, Estonia and Croatia, and K9 self-propelled howitzer supply contracts with Finland and Spain, expanding ground weapons exports beyond its earlier Poland-centered business. (Filing)

In August, the company was selected as a prototype supplier for the U.S. Army's next-generation self-propelled howitzer program, which the report says raises the possibility of K9 exports to the United States. Being a prototype supplier is a step toward a program of record, not a confirmed export order. (Reported)

What's still ahead

The Kiwoom report expects further export growth from Egypt and Australia, and says second-half growth will be driven by expanded K9 and Chunmoo deliveries to Poland. Kiwoom analyst Lee Han-gyeol cited a "solid order pipeline," including a third Poland contract and a Saudi Arabia ground forces program, as reasons the ground defense business should keep expanding. Neither the Poland third contract nor the Saudi program is described as signed. (Reported, forward-looking)

What could limit the upside

The report flags less favorable currency conditions in the second half compared to the first half, which it says could limit how much profitability improves even as revenue grows. (Reported)

Quick FAQ

Is the $4.5 trillion won operating profit figure confirmed?
No. It is Kiwoom Securities' full-year 2026 estimate, not company guidance or an actual reported result.

Has Hanwha Aerospace secured a U.S. export order for the K9?
Not yet. It was selected in August as a prototype supplier for the U.S. Army's next-generation self-propelled howitzer program, which raises the possibility of a future export order but is not itself a signed export deal.

Which export contracts are already signed?
Chunmoo supply contracts with Norway, Estonia and Croatia, and K9 supply contracts with Finland and Spain, are described as signed in 2026, alongside the existing Poland business.
